title: Mommy's Big Voice
vol: Mommy Is Human Too · Book Two
verse: "…let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath."

pages.text:
It started as a morning that was racing way too fast:
the toast was burnt, a shoe was lost, and time went speeding past.

Then Baby Bee spilled cereal. And Biscuit gave a bark.
The backpack wasn't ready and the car keys missed their mark.

And Pip had lost a single sock. And Jojo's work was due.
And every ticking second made the morning harder, too.

Inside, a little pressure started building up like steam —
a kettle getting hotter, getting ready now to scream.

She asked them, "Please get ready!" — once, then twice, then three, then four.
But no one seemed to hear her as the chaos grew some more.

And then it all came spilling out; she didn't mean to — but
out came Mommy's BIG LOUD VOICE, and every mouth went shut.

The kitchen went so quiet. Every little face went still.
And Baby Bee's small lip began to wobble, until —

— Mommy saw their great big eyes and felt her heart go small.
That was not the voice that she would ever choose at all.

She knelt down on the kitchen floor and took a breath, and then
she gathered up her children close and softly spoke again:

"I yelled, and that was wrong of me. The big loud voice was mine.
You didn't make me use it, and you didn't cross a line.

I let too many feelings build, and bubble up too fast,
so out they burst the loudest way. I'm sorry for the blast.

I'm learning, just like you are, how to hold a stormy day:
to breathe before I bubble up, and find a kinder way.

So when my voice grows big again — and yes, someday it will —
I'll catch it, say I'm sorry, and I'll hold you closer still."

Because your Mommy tries and trips and learns the whole day through —
and Mommy's voice gets big sometimes… because she's human too.

verses: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath.
Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.
He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.
Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.
